tools.name: diagnose_mortgage_comparison
tools.description: Use this first when a user wants a Canadian mortgage renewal, extra-payment, break-or-stay or debt-consolidation comparison but has not yet given the key figures. From the facts already supplied, returns the missing ones in priority order and up to three questions to ask (balance, rate, remaining amortization, term, switching costs, lender-quoted penalty). Flags a request to borrow additional cash (cash-out refinance) as unsupported. Do not use when the figures are already supplied: call the matching calculator. Does not calculate, rank, check qualification or search rates.

tools.name: compare_renewal_offers
tools.description: Use this when a user has two or three Canadian mortgage offers for the same balance, such as a renewal letter from the current lender and a quote to switch lender at renewal, and wants them compared. Compares the user-supplied rates, terms, amortizations, cashback and switching costs over a common horizon. Returns payments, interest, debt left, modeled borrowing cost and missing facts. Do not use for leaving a mortgage before the term ends (use compare_break_or_stay). Does not search or predict rates, confirm qualification or recommend a lender. An unknown cost is never treated as zero. Example: {"startingBalance":"412000","offers":[{"label":"Renewal","annualRatePercent":"4.89","convention":"nominal_semiannual","termMonths":60,"amortizationMonths":300,"frequency":"monthly","paymentMode":"recalculate_payment","costs":[]},{"label":"Switch","annualRatePercent":"4.59","convention":"nominal_semiannual","termMonths":60,"amortizationMonths":300,"frequency":"monthly","paymentMode":"recalculate_payment","costs":[]}]}

startingBalance.description: Mortgage balance now, in CAD: digits, optionally with a leading $ and thousands commas, for example "412000", "412000.50" or "$412,000". Before any costs are added.

annualRatePercent.description: Annual interest rate as a percent number, with or without a trailing % sign: 4.89% is "4.89", never "0.0489". Wrapped as a fact.

convention.description: Compounding convention of the quoted rate: nominal_semiannual or nominal_monthly. The mortgage documents state it. Mark unknown if the user has not said; do not guess.

termMonths.description: Term length in months, never years: a 5-year term is 60.

amortizationMonths.description: Remaining amortization in months, never years: 25 years is 300. Never inferred from the payment.

frequency.description: Payment frequency. biweekly is 26 payments a year sized to the stated amortization. accelerated_biweekly is the monthly payment divided by 2, paid 26 times a year, so more is paid each year. weekly and accelerated_weekly are the same idea with 52 payments and division by 4. "Every two weeks" alone does not say which: mark unknown or ask.

paymentMode.description: How the payment is set. recalculate_payment: the payment is calculated from the rate and amortization; use it for an ordinary mortgage, including a fixed-rate mortgage. fixed_payment: hold the dollar payment given in fixedPayment; it does not mean a fixed interest rate.

fixedPayment.description: Dollar payment per payment period in CAD. Needed only when paymentMode is fixed_payment.

tools.name: plan_mortgage_prepayments
tools.description: Use this when a user asks what paying extra on one Canadian mortgage would do: a higher regular payment, recurring extra payments, or up to 50 lump sums. Compares the supplied mortgage with and without the extras: interest, debt left and modeled payoff period. Checks the extras against prepayment-privilege limits only when the user supplies them; otherwise reports the limits as not checked. Do not use to find a prepayment penalty or the cost of breaking a mortgage: no tool calculates a penalty, the lender quotes it. Results beyond the term need explicit monthly continuation assumptions. tools.name: compare_break_or_stay
tools.description: Use this when a user is partway through a Canadian mortgage term and asks whether to break the mortgage early (to refinance the same debt, switch lender or take a lower rate) or stay until the term ends. Compares keeping it with a user-supplied replacement offer, counting the lender-quoted penalty, such as an interest rate differential (IRD) or three months' interest. Shows cashflow payback separately from borrowing-cost crossover. Do not use to calculate or estimate a penalty: the lender must quote it, and an unknown penalty prevents an unconditional ranking. No cash-out or rate search. tools.name: compare_debt_consolidation
tools.description: Use this when a user asks about rolling other debts into a Canadian mortgage (debt consolidation), for example credit-card, car-loan or existing line-of-credit or HELOC balances, each entered with a fixed monthly payment or as interest-only. Compares three scenarios over a common horizon: keep the mortgage and debts, consolidate at the new minimum payment, and consolidate while keeping the same monthly repayment budget. Shows interest, debt left, fees and limits. Monthly mortgage payments only; 1 to 10 debts. Do not use for a new HELOC, additional cash-out or qualification: none is modeled. monthlyPayment.description: Set monthly payment of a fixed_monthly debt, in CAD. For an interest_only debt use {state:"unknown"}: the payment modeled is each month's interest.

type.description: fixed_monthly for a debt with a set monthly payment; interest_only for a balance such as a line of credit that pays interest only.

annualRatePercent.description: Annual interest rate as a percent number, with or without a trailing % sign: 4.89% is "4.89", never "0.0489". Wrapped as a fact.

convention.description: Compounding convention of the quoted rate: nominal_semiannual or nominal_monthly. The mortgage documents state it. Mark unknown if the user has not said; do not guess.

termMonths.description: Term length in months, never years: a 5-year term is 60.

amortizationMonths.description: Remaining amortization in months, never years: 25 years is 300. Never inferred from the payment.

frequency.description: Payment frequency. biweekly is 26 payments a year sized to the stated amortization. accelerated_biweekly is the monthly payment divided by 2, paid 26 times a year, so more is paid each year. weekly and accelerated_weekly are the same idea with 52 payments and division by 4. "Every two weeks" alone does not say which: mark unknown or ask.

horizonMonths.description: Comparison horizon in months. Defaults to the shortest supplied term, at most 120.

monthlyBudget.description: Total monthly amount the user wants to keep paying after consolidating. Defaults to the current mortgage payment plus the debt payments due in month one.

perEventCap.description: Per-payment prepayment limit in CAD. Omitted means the contract has no per-payment limit; {state:"unknown"} means a limit may exist, so limits are not checked.

annualCap.description: Annual prepayment limit in CAD. Omitted means the contract has no dollar annual limit; {state:"unknown"} means a limit may exist, so limits are not checked. With a percentage basis, a supplied amount is also checked and the stricter applies; an absolute basis requires this amount.

basis.description: Basis of the annual limit: absolute uses annualCap; original_principal and current_balance use percentage.

resetMonth.description: Month whose first day starts each prepayment year.

percentage.description: Annual prepayment limit as a percent number in a string: 15% is "15". Used with basis original_principal or current_balance.

startDate.description: Date of period 0; due dates follow the illustrative calendar.

tools.name: get_mortgage_guide
tools.description: Use this when a user asks how to prepare for or understand a supported Canadian mortgage topic and is not asking for a calculation: renewal, switching costs, unequal terms, payment versus cost, renewal checklist, prepayments, break or stay, debt consolidation, or the calculation method. Returns one short, dated preparation guide written for Ontario and reviewed by an Ontario mortgage agent, with its public source, review status and follow-up questions. Do not use for general financial, legal or tax advice, current rates, arbitrary URLs or live web search. Example: {"topic":"renewal"}

topic.description: One of the nine guide topics.

detail.description: brief returns the first two sentences; full returns the whole guide.
